General fixes

2. Build flavor first - just as you would brown beef for stew, saute onions, garlic, spices and a spoon of tomato paste before adding them. Blooming spices matters even more in plant-based dishes.
3. Layer smartly - dense roots (potatoes, carrots, sweet potatoes) on the bottom, and cut everything to a similar size.
4. Add delicate ingredients late - spinach, peas, zucchini, coconut milk, dairy and fresh herbs in the last 15-30 minutes.
5. Do not lift the lid - each peek adds roughly 15-20 minutes.

7. Know your cooker - many models run hot; if food is mushy or dry, shorten the time or use LOW.

Plant-based specifics
- Red lentils break down in about 3-4 hours on low; green or brown lentils hold their shape better. Do not overcook them.
- Soak dried beans, and boil red kidney beans hard for at least 10 minutes first (a slow cooker does not get hot enough to destroy their natural toxin). If beans stay hard, add tomatoes and other acidic ingredients later.

Yogurt
- Use a thermometer: heat the milk to 180-185F, then cool it to 110-115F before adding the starter. Too hot kills the cultures; too cool gives runny yogurt.
- Use fresh plain yogurt with live cultures (about 2 tbsp per quart), whisk gently, then incubate with the cooker off, wrapped in towels (or in the oven with the light on), undisturbed for 8-12 hours.

Cashew yogurt
- Do not heat it to 180F like dairy; just warm it to about 110F and use a vegan starter or probiotic capsules.
- Blend the soaked cashews until very smooth and use less water for a thicker result. Straining removes body, so only strain if it is grainy. It thickens more as it chills.
